newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to import cooking oil - press.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to import cooking oil - press.

text.p: Indonesia's National Logistic Agency (Bulog) plans to import cooking oil to curb domestic price increases, the Jakarta Post reported on Monday.

The daily quoted a Bulog statement at the weekend as saying the agency would purchase cooking oil on the international market because local crude palm oil (CPO) producers were unlikely to be able to meet domestic demand.
"Bulog predicts that it will have to import cooking oil in the next few months owing to a lack of CPO stocks at state-owned palm oil producers," the paper said.
Bulog said in July and August, local producers exported most of their CPO because of higher prices and low export taxes.

The increase in exports boosted domestic cooking oil prices to a peak of 1,500 rupiah per kg in late August from 1,310 rupiah to 1,315 rupiah in late July. Bulog normally buys CPO, the raw material for cooking oil, rather than finished cooking oil as part of its buffer-stock strategy.
The CPO is later processed by local refiners.

The Jakarta Post said actual CPO production in July and the estimated August figure was 400,000 tonnes and 415,000 tonnes respectively, lower than initial projections of 415,000 tonnes and 455,000 tonnes.
Traders had expected firm olein and CPO prices to continue until the end of August as local supply would remain tight in the wake of increased exports this month.
